summary: We developed SPHEREx Sky Explorer, a web-based astronomical platform built with FastAPI, Astropy, and Three.js that makes NASA’s SPHEREx infrared survey instantly accessible. The platform addresses the challenge of navigating complex Multi-Extension FITS files by connecting directly to Caltech/IPAC IRSA archives. It automates WCS North-Up reprojection, multi-epoch blinking, moving object differencing (B−AB - A), and point-source kinematic tracking, while cross-matching sources with Gaia DR3 and AllWISE catalogs. It also reconstructs 102-band infrared spectra (0.75–5.00 μm) and renders interactive 3D hyperspectral data cubes. By removing heavy desktop software barriers and introducing a bilingual (English/Myanmar) interface, our system empowers both astronomers and citizen scientists to explore the dynamic infrared cosmos.
details:
Project Details
1. What does it do & How does it work?
SPHEREx Sky Explorer is a web-based platform that makes NASA’s SPHEREx infrared survey accessible to everyone through a "Learn First, Explore Next" model:
Interactive Learning Pages: Interactive 3D modules explain celestial coordinates (RA/DEC), SPHEREx’s 102 infrared bands, the Caltech/IPAC IRSA pipeline, North-Up WCS alignment, and aperture photometry before users use the tools.
Analysis Tools:
Track: Measures point-source kinematics (proper motion in mas/yr\text{mas/yr}, displacement, light curves) and features a personal "Nickname Studio" watchlist.
Explore: Blinks multi-epoch visits, creates deep coadded stacks, and detects moving objects via image differencing (B−AB - A).
Catalog: Overlays ESA Gaia DR3 and NASA AllWISE reference sources with dynamic proper motion vector arrows.
Spectrum: Extracts 102-band spectrophotometric SEDs (0.75−5.00 μm0.75 - 5.00\,\mu\text{m}) and visualizes them in an interactive Three.js 3D hyperspectral cube.
Under the Hood: A FastAPI/Astropy backend queries Caltech/IPAC IRSA TAP endpoints, processes Multi-Extension FITS (MEF) cutouts, subtracts zodiacal light (ZODI), masks bad pixels, and reprojects images to standard North-Up WCS grids in real time.

2. How is your project creative?
"Learn First" Pipeline: Most SPHEREx tools are complex and intimidating. We demystify advanced astrophysics first through interactive 3D WebGL models (orbit physics, 102 spectral bands, aperture zones) so anyone can understand the science before analyzing raw data.
Dual-Language Accessibility (English & Myanmar): The platform features a fully localized bilingual interface (English and Myanmar Unicode), bringing NASA data to underrepresented Southeast Asian communities.
Interactive "Nickname Studio": Allows users to click any star, assign custom nicknames, label categories (e.g., Brown Dwarf, Planet X Candidate), and track real motion over time.
Dual 2D/3D Spectrophotometry: Combines an interactive 2D SED curve (identifying H2O\text{H}_2\text{O}, CH4\text{CH}_4, and CO2\text{CO}_2 molecules) with an interactive 3D hyperspectral volumetric data cube.

3. What benefits does it have?
Zero Installation: Runs entirely in modern web browsers without heavy desktop software (DS9, TOPCAT) or Python environment setups.
Automated Data Processing: Instantly performs WCS reprojection, cosmic ray masking, zodiacal subtraction, and aperture photometry.
Resilient & Fast: Built-in HTTP retry strategies and intelligent disk caching shield users from NASA/IPAC 503 timeouts and rate limits.

4. What is the intended impact?
Democratizing Space Science: Empowers students, educators, and amateur astronomers worldwide to analyze real NASA survey data.
Citizen Science Discoveries: Enables crowdsourced discovery of fast-moving asteroids, cold brown dwarfs, and infrared transients.
Educational Inclusivity: Bridges the language barrier in astronomy education by offering the first bilingual SPHEREx platform.

5. Tools, Coding Languages & Data Sources
Languages: Python 3, JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3.
Backend: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Astropy, Astroquery, Reproject, Photutils, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, Pillow, Requests.
Frontend: Vanilla JavaScript, Three.js (r128), Three.js OrbitControls, HTML5 Canvas 2D API.
Data & APIs: NASA/IPAC IRSA TAP & IBE Cutout Service, ESA Gaia DR3, NASA AllWISE, CDS VizieR.
Fonts: Google Fonts (Lora, Silkscreen, Noto Sans Myanmar).

6. Factors Considered
API Rate Limits & Latency: Capped cutout requests to safe limits (≤20\le 20), added exponential backoff retries, and cached benchmark targets on disk.
Browser Performance: Used a single shared WebGL renderer with IntersectionObserver to prevent browser crashes from context exhaustion.
Visual Clarity: Implemented an adaptive AsinhStretch (1st–99.5th percentile) so faint nebulosity and bright stellar cores are visible simultaneously.
